definitions.explanation: An object that has been stolen, viewed especially from a legal or law-enforcement perspective. Knowingly buying, selling, or possessing such items is itself a crime.

examples.japanese: {盗品|とうひん}を{発見|はっけん}した。
この{店|みせ}は{盗品|とうひん}を{売|う}っていた{疑|うたが}いがある。
examples.english: This shop is suspected of selling stolen goods.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{倉庫|そうこ}から{大量|たいりょう}の{盗品|とうひん}を{押収|おうしゅう}した。
examples.english: The police confiscated a large quantity of stolen goods from the warehouse.

notes:
Compound of {盗|とう} (steal) + {品|ひん} (goods, item). A formal/legal term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {盗品|とうひん}を{売|う}る: to sell stolen goods
- {盗品|とうひん}を{買|か}う: to buy stolen goods
- {盗品|とうひん}を{押収|おうしゅう}する: to confiscate stolen goods
- {盗品|とうひん}と{知|し}って: knowing it is stolen

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {贓物|ぞうぶつ}: stolen property — archaic legal term, rarely used today
- {盗難品|とうなんひん}: item lost to theft — emphasizes the victim's perspective
